title: Bedtime Stories
cn: 第 11 集 · 睡前故事
novel:
During the long car ride from Minnesota to New York, Marshall [[recited|recite]] three rhyming [[tales|tale]] to baby Marvin. He hoped the [[rhythm|rhythm]] of the verses would help his tired son fall asleep on the road.

The first tale was about Ted and his [[adventures|adventure]] in New York. Marshall [[described|describe]] how Ted searched for love in the big city. He told the story in a [[funny|funny]] rhyme that made even Daphne laugh. Ted met many women, but none of them were the right one, until he finally found the mother of his children.

The second tale was about Barney and his [[legendary|legendary]] [[skills|skill]] at picking up women. Marshall rhymed about Barney's suits and his many [[conquests|conquest]]. The story was [[exaggerated|exaggerate]] for comedy, but it captured Barney's spirit perfectly. Marvin seemed to enjoy the silly voices Marshall used for each [[character|character]].

The third tale was about Marshall himself. He told Marvin about how he met Lily, fell in love, and started a family. This tale was the most [[personal|personal]] and heartfelt. Marshall's voice grew [[softer|soft]] as he described the day Marvin was born. He told his son that being a father was the greatest [[journey|journey]] of his life.

By the end of the third tale, Marvin was finally asleep. Daphne, who had been listening quietly, was [[touched|touch]] by Marshall's stories. She told him he was a good father. Marshall smiled, feeling [[grateful|grateful]] for his family and the long trip that brought him to this moment.

recite.en: She recited a poem from memory.

tale.en: He told a tale of adventure.

rhythm.en: The song has a good rhythm.

skill.en: She has great skill in cooking.

soft.en: She spoke in a soft voice.

journey.en: The journey was long but worth it.

grateful.en: She was grateful for the help.
